Harper Lin: Heads-up: canary showed a billing spike tied to WS reconnects. Looks like sessions survive a proxy half-close and keep counting tokens.
Chen Wu: Repro steps?
Harper Lin: Open WS, stream, inject FIN on proxy (tc qdisc/netem) so client reconnects to different edge. New session accepted, old one never GCs.
Amaya Singh: Do we rely on close callbacks to decrement in-flight? If EOF not surfaced, finalizer won't run.
Harper Lin: Exactly. Edge logs show accept on new shard and no close event for old shard. Snippet:
```
INFO 2026-03-22T09:11:02Z accept resume shard=us-east-1 resume_id=rs_77a last_event=204
INFO 2026-03-22T09:11:02Z accept resume shard=us-west-2 resume_id=rs_77a last_event=204
```
Chen Wu: Two shards owning same resume -> double in-flight counters. Do we have leases/tombstones?
Amaya Singh: We use a session-lease TTL=30s and tombstones, but lease refresh and GC can race when reconnects are fast.
Harper Lin: Short-term mitigation: console should dedupe active sessions by (tenant,resume_id) within 60s to avoid alert storms. Long-term: we need backend reconciliation.
Chen Wu: Proposal: keep optimistic increment at accept, spawn async reconciler that does a CAS on central metadata. If CAS fails, emit quota_compensation event for billing pipeline.
Amaya Singh: Add metric ws_reconcile_conflict{shard,tenant} and a tracing span on reconcile path. Also include claim_nonce in logs to correlate which accept won.
infra-bot: Note: lowering lease TTL may reduce window but risks false GC on slow clients.
deploy-bot: Rolling patch: async-reconciler -> canary us-east in 15m.
ops-bot: Ticket INF-9124 created: "console: transient dedupe for active sessions (tenant,resume_id,60s)" assigned to Amaya.
Harper Lin: Action items: 1) reconciler PR (Chen) 2) claim_nonce logs + metric (Chen/Harper) 3) console dedupe (Amaya) 4) monitor ws_reconcile_conflict on canary (ops).
Chen Wu: I'll send small PR for claim_nonce today.
Amaya Singh: I'll make console change non-destructive (only suppress alerts).
Harper Lin: Thanks, will post canary results here. :rocket:
